text_to_image: First-person perspective. The protagonist is holding a small mechanical toy in one hand. Below the hand is a wooden table that fully covers the background. The toy is small enough to fit perfectly in one hand and is currently in its untransformed state. It is a compact, teardrop puck-shaped object made of blackened steel and burnished brass, interlocking brass gears and micro-pistons. The toy features a tiny copper disc nestled in the tail curve. Soft diffused daylight from the upper left, shallow depth of field. Photorealistic, ultra-detailed, high quality.
image_to_video: First-person perspective, filmed in one continuous long take, strictly no cuts or camera transitions allowed. The camera remains steady and does not move. The protagonist presses the tiny copper disc nestled in the tail curve with their finger, then places the toy onto the wooden table below. The transformation begins immediately and completes fully within the shot. The toy begins unfolding and transforming until it becomes the form of a miniature mechanical scorpion. The unfolding and transformation process is logical and physically consistent. The smooth top plating splits along a central seam and swings open to form segmented armor plates, revealing the movement of internal mechanical components and gears. Eight jointed legs, two articulated pincers, and a curved stinger tail physically push out into place. The transformation process is relatively simple and not overly complicated. Strictly no parts appear or disappear out of nowhere. After transformation, the final mechanical scorpion's size remains believable and perfectly consistent with what the original toy could realistically unfold into, with absolutely no magical volume expansion. Audio: crisp mechanical clicks, servo whirs and ratcheting gears, ending with a soft metallic latch as the transformation completes. No music, no voice.
